hard_gates.gate: G1 gate catches leaks planted in p00's kernel surface
hard_gates.evidence: Plants are in plants/plants.diff, gated by CRITIC_PLANT and run in the toolbox with plants/run-plants.sh. odoo.task: sign-in (sign in to an empty workspace)
odoo.notes: Command: COMPARE_OURS_URL=http://localhost:20050 node run.mjs --task sign-in --product both --repeat 3, against the odoo-reference rig on :8069 (100,000-row volume confirmed live). All 6 runs were verified. Ours was judged on one whole path, 'passkey': on a device that has used a passkey, the screen asks for it as it opens, from any address, and the person confirms once. Odoo's best path is 'Use a Passkey' then confirm. Its login asset binds the passkey request only to a click on .passkey_login_link; nothing asks on load. Results: steps 1<2, machine 0.094<1.296 s, KLM 2.03<4.68 s, human+wait 2.12<5.89 s. Keystrokes were 0 in both and were left out (needs-human #11). Ours' password paths, judged against Odoo's best metrics, lose on their own: new-device 4 steps/35 keys, whole-e-mail 3/56, returning 2/21. Blind shots: compare/blind/shots (4 kept; 8 other runs' shots deleted to stay within 12 screenshots).

biggest_gap.title: The sign-in win rests on the passkey path alone; signing in with a password ties Odoo on the plain address, and on a shared PC it loses
biggest_gap.detail: Ours beats Odoo only when the person already uses a passkey on this device: 1 confirmation against Odoo's 2 steps. Every first sign-in uses a password, and so does every staff member on a shared counter or warehouse PC. On that path the result is a tie or a loss. (1) Plain address '/': typing a whole e-mail does not move on to the password, so the path is e-mail, Enter, password, Enter: 4 steps and 57 keys for admin@alnoor.example. Odoo's e-mail, Tab, password, Enter is the same 4 steps and 57 keys. Ours wins only on machine seconds. This is round 7's gap, still open. (2) A shared device where anyone once used a passkey (erp.passkeyOffer=1): as the screen opens, it starts a passkey request for up to 300 s, and while that runs the 'Sign in' button is disabled. The page cannot abort the request, so a typed e-mail, Enter, password, Enter does nothing. The next person must first cancel the system prompt: 5 steps against Odoo's 4. For a UAE trading company with shared PCs at the counter and in the warehouse, this is the common case. The fix should let the password path win without a passkey, and must never let the passkey offer block it. Options: abort the arrival request as soon as the person types in the e-mail field (AbortController) and keep Sign in enabled; offer the passkey as a conditional/autofill request (mediation: 'conditional') rather than a modal; move on to the password once the e-mail's domain matches a known workspace on the plain address.
biggest_gap.evidence: attack/shared-device.mjs and shared-device.txt (screenshot 10-shared-device-password-blocked.png): a context with localStorage erp.passkeyOffer=1 and a platform authenticator holding no passkey of this person. On arrival '#passkey-asking' is shown. After typing admin@alnoor.example, Enter, Demo-Pass-2026, Enter, the person is still not signed in after 15 s. web/src/modules/shell/SignInPage.tsx line 417: disabled={busy || asking}. There is no AbortController in SignInPage.tsx or kernel/passkeys.ts. GET /api/auth/session returns passkey.timeout 300000. browser-notes.txt part 2 shows that on plain '/', focus stays in the e-mail field after a whole e-mail is typed. compare/comparisons/sign-in.json gives ours' password paths: new-device 4 steps/35 keys, whole-e-mail 3/56 (team address only), returning 2/21. To reproduce, ./erp up, then node attack/shared-device.mjs against http://localhost:<port>.

other_findings: The one command depends on machine load. On the owner's PC, with four pieces' critics at once (load up to 85), ./erp verify passed every test and still failed on processor time: 11,671 s against the 10,500 s maximum. The .NET stage alone used 9,753 s. The same commit used 8,694 s at load 2 to 40, and the integrator measured 7,972 s. With seven pieces still to add tests, the margin is about 17% on a quiet machine and negative on a busy one. The .NET stage's processor cost is the lever.

G1 non-interference cannot see side channels carried by the database. It compares answers from two app processes over the same database, so anything read from PostgreSQL's shared statistics or catalogs (pg_stat_user_tables.n_live_tup, pg_class.reltuples), which erp_app can read for every table, looks identical in both processes. Plant L3 (a list total taken from n_live_tup) was caught only by the HTTP attack's list-walk check. That check fires because the plant changes total without changing the rows. A plant that leaked a whole-database figure somewhere else (an 'activity' counter, a grouping count) would rely on that check alone. Hardening: revoke erp_app's SELECT on the statistics views, or check in the gate that the app role cannot read other tenants' row counts from the catalogs, and add a static ban on pg_stat_* and reltuples in product code.

Every critic plant was caught: L1 (raw xmin versions) by G1RowVersionTests, L3 by G1HttpIsolationTests, P1 (read implied by any same-resource permission) by G2 grant-exactly-one, and P2 (no requirement for read permissions) by the host's start-up check. The HTTP isolation test alone took 38 minutes in the planted gate run.

Keyboard (round 7's finding, still open): in the shell, Tab after the last navigation link ('My account') lands on the document body before 'Skip to content', a dead stop each cycle (browser-notes.txt part 2). Keyboard sign-in works in English and Arabic. The Arabic shell is RTL with lang=ar. Its only Latin text is company codes, 'Ctrl', the 'English' switch and the workspace code.

Sign-in lockout (round 7's finding, still open): after 8 failures, the right password still gets only the generic 'Sign-in failed. Check your e-mail and password and try again.', with no hint that the account is paused or for how long (browser-notes.txt).

A passkey added on My account works: a fresh visit to the plain address on that device signs in with no key in 371 ms, recorded as a successful sign-in and audited (insert into identity.passkeys with actor). An empty workspace provisioned in Arabic signs in by keyboard in 0.82 s to an RTL home (09-empty-workspace-first-sign-in.jpg).
